rows.description: A preschooler presses the lips tightly to refuse food or medicine, signalling a wish for control. Offering a limited choice usually works better than force.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child clenches the jaw during a strong tantrum, a sign of overwhelming anger or effort to hold back. Calm presence and a quiet space help the body settle.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, calm, overwhelm

rows.description: A preschooler sticks out the tongue at a sibling as teasing, while another child does it in play. Adults teach kind alternatives when it is meant to insult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child sees an adult's neutral face and wrongly reads anger or dislike. Adults can say they are just thinking, and children learn a face is not always a mood.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler tries to keep a straight face in games like statue or staring contests, practising control of the face. It is fun, and stopping at any sign of distress keeps it safe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child lowers the head after doing something wrong or when embarrassed, showing shame or fear. Kind correction helps the child learn without feeling worthless.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, shame, embarrassment

rows.description: A preschooler nods to agree or answer, although a nod may just mean I heard you rather than I agree. Adults confirm understanding with a question.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler shrugs to mean I do not know or I do not mind, copying adults. It can also be a way to avoid answering, and gentle prompts help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child holds the shoulders tight before saying something in class, showing nervousness. Slow breaths and a friendly nod from the teacher help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, relief from stress

rows.description: A preschooler folds the arms and looks away when upset, a sign of sulking or refusal, though a child may also fold arms because of cold or comfort. Asking is wiser than assuming defiance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
